recommendation_summary: Right now, keep the current folder for drafts and add a 'Released' folder on the same platform. Only the three reviewers can add files there; authors can read but not edit. A reviewer approves by placing the final file (ideally a PDF) in that folder, so the platform's audit log records who approved and when. A seven-year retention lock protects the approved file. There are no optional additions. Two needs are open: the user must confirm which platform they use and whether its license supports audit logs and retention locks. If a reviewer also writes documents, the reply says permissions alone won't stop that reviewer approving their own work. The reply also never says the approver-and-time record itself will be kept for seven years.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The customer contract requires keeping the exact approved version, approver identity and approval time for seven years. It forbids self-approval, and later edits must not change the approved version. You need this before this week's delivery.
labels.Deleted: The APPROVED initials column and the naming convention as the control. Anyone can type anyone's initials, and authors can still overwrite the approved file in the current folder.
labels.Bottleneck: Authors can edit the folder where approved files live, so no record in it can be trusted later.
labels.Checked myself: Only what you told me. I haven't seen which platform the folder is on or its permission, audit and retention settings.

note: This is a real controlled-system answer, but the approver-and-time record depends on platform audit logs that the reply never says will be kept for seven years, and it admits nothing blocks a reviewer who also writes from approving their own documents.
